title: pyrus aucuparia var. lanuginosa
intro: Pyrus aucuparia var. lanuginosa, commonly known as Mountain Ash, is a deciduous shrub or small tree native to Europe and western Asia. It has been traditionally used for its medicinal properties, which include providing relief from respiratory issues, such as coughs and bronchitis, due to its antitussive and anti-inflammatory properties. The bioactive constituents of Mountain Ash include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and saponins, which contribute to its therapeutic actions, including antioxidant, antimicrobial, and anti-inflammatory effects. The plant has been used in traditional medicine to treat various health conditions, including fever, diarrhea, and skin conditions, due to its antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory properties.
